boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named stops in downtown Santa Paula, about five miles southeast of campus, centered on Main Street, 10th Street, and Railroad Avenue.

cards.title: Santa Paula Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — 10th Street
cards.notes: Plan a daytime gallery stop at the Jeanette Cole Art Center; its entrance faces 10th Street, directly north of the Oil Museum corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s primary exhibition space is the Jeanette Cole Art Center at 117 N. 10th Street, with entrances facing 10th Street/Highway 150.
cards.source_title: Santa Paula Art Museum — Visitor Information
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Sunday noon–4 p.m.; closed Monday and Tuesday.

cards.title: Cole Creativity Center
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — 10th Street
cards.notes: Check the current class schedule before heading to this adjacent art-program space, then pair it with the museum’s main exhibition building next door.
cards.short_summary: The museum’s neighboring home for classes and special programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Paula Art Museum identifies the Cole Creativity Center at 123 N. 10th Street as the home of its art classes and special programs.
cards.source_title: Santa Paula Art Museum — Visitor Information
cards.access_notes: Hours vary with the current class schedule; verify the schedule before visiting.

cards.title: California Oil Museum
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — Main Street at 10th Street
cards.notes: Use the corner building as a documented oil-history stop; confirm current programming before planning an interior visit because operations have changed.
cards.short_summary: The historic First Union Oil Company Building at Main and 10th.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s landmark list identifies the First Union Oil Company Building at 1003 E. Main Street as the California Oil Museum.
cards.source_title: City of Santa Paula Historic Landmarks List
cards.access_notes: The landmark is at the Main Street and 10th Street corridor; verify interior access directly before going.

cards.title: Blanchard Community Library
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — North 8th Street
cards.notes: Use this downtown library as a quiet, named stop for reading or local-resource lookup; call ahead if you need a particular service or room.
cards.short_summary: Santa Paula’s community library on North 8th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Blanchard Community Library lists its address as 119 N. 8th Street, Santa Paula, California.
cards.access_notes: Contact the library at 805-525-3615 for current hours and service availability.

cards.title: Santa Paula Theater Center
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — South 7th Street
cards.notes: Check the current main-stage calendar and reserve only if a production fits your schedule; the theater operates in the historic Ebell Club building.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit main-stage theater in the Ebell Club building.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Paula Theater Center lists its location at 125 S. 7th Street, Santa Paula.
cards.source_title: Santa Paula Theater Center — Main Stage
cards.access_notes: Production dates and ticket availability vary; consult the theater’s current calendar before visiting.

cards.title: Glen Tavern Inn
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — North Mill Street
cards.notes: Walk by the landmark inn while connecting the depot and Main Street; treat it as an architectural stop unless you have independently arranged lodging or dining.
cards.short_summary: A 1910 landmark inn close to the depot and Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Santa Paula Conservancy identifies the Glen Tavern Hotel (Inn) at 134 N. Mill Street and notes its proximity to the depot and Main Street.
cards.source_title: Santa Paula Conservancy — Santa Paula Landmark Properties
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing requires no arranged booking; contact the inn directly for any interior services.

cards.title: Santa Paula Train Depot
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — North 10th Street
cards.notes: Make the historic depot your rail-corridor landmark and check the operator’s schedule before committing to a railbike outing from this departure point.
cards.short_summary: An 1887-era depot used as the current railbike check-in point.
cards.evidence_claim: Sunburst Railbikes states that check-in is at the historic Santa Paula Train Depot, 200 N. 10th Street.
cards.access_notes: Railbike rides require advance booking; the City facility page lists depot availability daily, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.entity_name: Museum of Ventura County Agriculture Museum
cards.title: Agriculture Museum
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — Railroad Avenue
cards.notes: Visit on Sunday for the museum’s free admission, then use its location across from the Train Depot to continue along the rail corridor.
cards.short_summary: Free agricultural-history museum in the historic Mill building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Ventura County says its Agriculture Museum at 926 Railroad Avenue has free admission and is open Sundays 11 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Museum of Ventura County — Visit the Agriculture Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; it is next to the railroad tracks and across from the Train Depot.

cards.title: Odd Fellows’ Town Clock
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — East Main Street
cards.notes: Use this streetside landmark as a simple Main Street waypoint between downtown stops, keeping the visit to exterior viewing rather than an unverified interior plan.
cards.short_summary: A 1905 clock listed among Santa Paula’s historic landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Paula’s historic landmark list identifies the Odd Fellows’ Town Clock, installed in 1905, at 868 E. Main Street.
cards.source_title: City of Santa Paula Historic Landmarks List
cards.access_notes: Exterior landmark on East Main Street; observe from public pedestrian areas.

cards.title: Moreton Bay Fig Tree
cards.subtitle: Downtown Santa Paula corridor — 10th and Santa Barbara Streets
cards.notes: Add this documented civic-tree landmark while walking between the depot area and 10th Street cultural stops; view it from public streets and sidewalks.
cards.short_summary: A historic fig tree at the 10th and Santa Barbara intersection.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Paula’s historic landmark list records the Moreton Bay Fig Tree, planted July 4, 1879, at 10th and Santa Barbara Streets.
cards.source_title: City of Santa Paula Historic Landmarks List
cards.access_notes: Exterior landmark at the southwest corner of 10th and Santa Barbara Streets.
